**Observations:**
- Tomato leaf with numerous small-to-medium circular dark brown/black spots scattered across the entire surface
- Many spots have a slightly lighter center with a distinct dark border — classic pycnidia pattern
- General yellowing (chlorosis) of the leaf tissue surrounding the spots
- Spots are fairly uniform in shape, roughly circular, not forming large irregular blotches
- No concentric "target" rings typical of Early Blight; no large water-soaked lesions typical of Late Blight

**Reasoning:**
The dense distribution of small circular lesions with dark borders and faintly lighter centers containing pycnidia is the hallmark of **Septoria lycopersici** (Septoria Leaf Blotch) on tomato. Bacterial Speck produces much tinier specks with pronounced yellow halos. Early Blight produces larger target-ring lesions. The pattern here — numerous, evenly distributed, small circular spots on a yellowing leaf — fits Septoria Leaf Blotch most closely.
